toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The departures are concentrated in one place. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel have resigned, against 1 of the 13 who never worked on it. Pay, the firm-wide hours target and ordinary market movement apply to everyone in the group, so they cannot explain that gap. A £12k payment for all 19 associates (about £228k) is therefore unlikely to fix the problem, and closing the review on that basis would be a mistake. I'd advise against it.

What we can't yet tell is whether the cause is the Kestrel workload or the way Dorian Faulk supervises. Every Kestrel associate reports to him, and he supervises no one else. The survey comments mention both weekend work and humiliating late-night corrections, but they don't say which drives people to leave. I'm fairly confident about the Kestrel concentration and unsure about the cause within it.

Next steps: commission the external confidential interviews (about £9k, and four leavers have already agreed). Design them to separate supervision from workload. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Hold off on moving supervision or hiring contract reviewers until the interviews are done. Document review ends in December, so don't wait long.
output.methodChoice: Collected X11 only (matter and supervising-partner split of departures); stopped since the other items were unlikely to separate supervision from workload.
